page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5ne.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, and network performance is defined by a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the ecs.g5ne.2xlarge sits primarily in the lower performance tiers for modern workloads. Single-core and multi-core CPU benchmarks, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, register in the bottom 25% of tested instances. Memory read bandwidth is also relatively weak, though large-block write bandwidth and Passmark CPU extended instructions achieve average tier results. Redis SET operations perform moderately well, processing 5.91 million operations per second. Small LLM inference tasks show average throughput, but larger models result in poor performance.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio, this instance offers a stable environment for legacy workloads that do not require high-performance compute or local storage. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the hardware represents an older generation Intel platform, making it suitable for predictable, non-burstable workloads where cost-to-resource density is prioritized over raw processing speed. Appropriate workloads include moderate web serving, Redis caching, and general-purpose application hosting.
